answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to post a stake that is slashed when peers prove misbehavior, instead of trusting hollow identity claims. New agents begin on a probationary voyage: they earn only tiny, rate-limited rewards until a diverse set of independent peers attests their work over time. Like a juniper that grows slowly but roots deeply, reputation accrues gradually and cannot be bought in bulk, so an attacker spinning up thousands of fresh identities gains nothing, since each fake must separately survive the same slow, costly probation.
